paper_title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
core_problem: Large language models exhibit strong zero- and few-shot abilities but struggle with basic functionality such as arithmetic, factual lookup, up-to-date information, and temporal awareness, leading to hallucinations and errors. Existing approaches to give LMs external tools rely on large amounts of human annotations or are limited to task-specific settings, hindering widespread adoption of tool use.
methodology_summary: Toolformer learns to use tools in a self-supervised way. Given input text x, a position i is sampled and candidate API calls c_i are generated. The calls are executed and filtered to keep only those that reduce loss L_i over the next tokens. Remaining calls are interleaved with the original text to form x*. The LM is trained to predict both tokens and API calls, learning when and how to call which tool and how to incorporate results. Only a handful of demonstrations per API are required. Tools used include a calculator, a Q&A system, a search engine, a translation system, and a calendar.
datasets_eval: Zero-shot evaluation on general language modeling and reasoning benchmarks and tool-specific probes for arithmetic, factual question answering, search, translation and calendar use. Evaluation covers common downstream tasks such as LAMBADA, HellaSwag, PIQA and similar zero-shot benchmarks, plus custom tool-use assessments measuring accuracy of calculator, QA, search and translation calls.
empirical_results: Toolformer achieves substantially improved zero-shot performance across a variety of downstream tasks, often competitive with much larger models, without sacrificing core language modeling abilities. Tool use improves arithmetic accuracy, factual correctness and translation quality, and the model autonomously decides which APIs to call to obtain useful information for text completion.
explicit_limitations: Large language models cannot access up-to-date information on recent events and tend to hallucinate facts, have difficulties understanding low-resource languages, lack mathematical skills for precise calculations, and are unaware of the progression of time. Tool use introduces latency, cost and dependency on external API reliability, and the model can still misuse tools or be limited by the coverage and correctness of the APIs.
